summary: A change notice from BBN for a new IMP system version. It raised the number of hosts one IMP can serve from three to four, collected more detailed statistics on host use for the Network Control Center, and changed the time unit of one timing statistic. BBN expected no direct effect on hosts.

plainLanguage.summary: The company that runs the network's switching boxes says it upgraded the box so it can plug in one more computer and keep better notes. Nobody should notice.

questions: imp host limit raised to four
subtitle: An announcement of IMP system version 2505 with expanded capacity and improved monitoring

tldr.problem: The ARPANET's IMP switching system had limitations in how many hosts one IMP could serve, and the Network Control Center (NCC) needed better visibility into host usage patterns.
tldr.mechanism: BBN deployed IMP system version 2505, which increased the number of hosts an IMP can handle from three to four, improved host statistics collection, and adjusted timing measurement units for more precise reporting.
tldr.outcome: The system expansion was transparent to hosts. The only external changes were one new status light and longer statistics reports that would now track a fourth host and measure round-trip time in more precise units.

today: This change notice exemplified BBN's role in maintaining and expanding the early ARPANET infrastructure, increasing capacity while preserving compatibility with existing host implementations.

sections.title: The Update
sections.content:
During the week of 16 August 1971, BBN installed a new version of the IMP system, version 2505. This update incorporated three principal changes to improve network capacity and monitoring.

The primary change was expanding the number of hosts the system could handle from three to four. Although this required significant internal changes to the IMP's host-handling routines, the only external effects were the presence of a new status light (light 8 monitors Host 4) and the lengthening of the 10-second and snapshot statistics reports.
sections.plainLanguage: An upgrade added room for one more computer to connect, with only a new indicator light to show the change on the outside.

sections.title: Improved Statistics
sections.content:
The host-handling routines were enhanced to gather more accurate and voluminous statistics on host usage of the network and report them to the Network Control Center. This gave the NCC better insight into how hosts were using network resources.

Additionally, the 10-second statistics were changed to measure the host "round trip" statistic in units of 800 microseconds rather than 100 microseconds. This change provided more precise timing measurements while consuming less space in the statistics reports.
sections.plainLanguage: The system now keeps better track of what each computer is doing and measures time more precisely.

sections.title: Impact on Hosts
sections.content: BBN anticipated that the new system should have no direct effect on the hosts themselves. The expansion and improvements were internal to the IMP infrastructure and should be transparent to host software and users. Hosts would continue to operate normally with the same interface and behavior.
sections.plainLanguage: Everything works the same from the host's point of view. The changes are all behind the scenes.
